panel.title: Kraftvakt
panel.not_loaded: Kraftvakt is not loaded. Check the integration under Settings → Devices & services.

status.stopped_info: The regulation is stopped, and all regulated appliances and EV chargers are turned off. The configuration can be changed. When the regulation starts, the appliances are turned on again one by one.
status.start_refused: The regulation cannot start before the configuration is complete.
status.safe_state_text: The power sensor {sensor} gives no valid measurement. All regulated appliances and EV chargers are turned off. The regulation starts again by itself when the sensor gives a valid value again.
status.safe_state_silent_text: The power sensor {sensor} has not reported for {timeout} s. All regulated appliances and EV chargers are turned off. The regulation starts again by itself when the sensor reports again.
status.penalty_text: The tariff average has been above the power limit. All regulated appliances and EV chargers are kept off until the overconsumption is recovered.
status.safe_state_back_text: The power sensor {sensor} gives a valid value again. The regulation starts again with everything off at the next decision.
status.no_chargers: No EV chargers in the group.
status.waiting_ends_at: Turns on at the decision at {time}
status.power_to_free_turn_on: {power} kW must be freed before it is turned on
status.power_to_free_activate: {power} kW must be freed before the EV charger is activated
status.power_to_free_ampere: {power} kW must be freed before the EV charger gets one more ampere
status.damping_ampere_at: One more ampere at the decision at {time}
status.start_delay_ends_at: Nothing below it is turned on before the decision at {time}
status.waiting_charger: Queued: another EV charger in the group has its turn
status.starting_until: Waiting until {time} for the car to start charging. Nothing below it is turned on until then.
status.activated_not_charging: Activated: the car does not use power, so it waits at the minimum current
status.regulation_stopped: The regulation is stopped, so the EV charger is deactivated
status.fault: A fault flag shows a fault, so the EV charger is deactivated until the fault clears
status.power_runs_out: The power runs out here. What is below waits for free power.
status.queued_for_room: Queued: waiting for room beside the EV chargers that charge
status.queued_waiting_time: Queued: next in turn, after its waiting time

diagnostics.chart_label: Consumption, regulation average, tariff average and power limit over the last hour
diagnostics.lanes_label: What each appliance and EV charger was set to, in priority order
diagnostics.no_events: No commands or failed actions are kept.
diagnostics.log_kept: The commands of the decisions kept, and the last failed actions. Kept until Home Assistant restarts or the integration is reloaded.
diagnostics.download: Download diagnostics on the integration's page

missing.missing_power_sensor: The power sensor is not chosen.
missing.missing_entity: {item}: the switch or thermostat is not chosen.
missing.missing_on_off_entity: {item}: the switch that turns charging on and off is not chosen.
missing.appliance_without_entity: An appliance without a switch or thermostat
missing.charger_without_device: An EV charger without a device

config.fix_before_saving: Fix the marked settings before saving.
config.not_saved: The configuration was not saved. Fix the marked settings.
config.save_refused_running: The configuration cannot be saved while the regulation runs.
config.leave_text: The changes on the configuration pages are not saved. They are lost if you leave.

locked.title: The configuration is locked
locked.text: The regulation runs. Stop the regulation to change the configuration. When the regulation stops, all regulated appliances and EV chargers are turned off.

warning.appliances_title: Do not turn regulated appliances on or off outside Kraftvakt
warning.chargers_title: Do not turn EV chargers on or off outside Kraftvakt
warning.text: It disturbs the regulation, and Kraftvakt sets them back. Turn on the switch «excluded from regulation» for one you want to control yourself.

errors.fault_flag_required: Choose a fault flag, or turn the setting off.
errors.duplicate_label: The label must be unique for the appliance.
errors.duplicate_name: The name is already used by another group.
errors.min_current_above_max: The minimum current cannot be above the maximum current.
errors.window_start_equals_end: Start and end cannot be the same.
errors.duplicate_entity: The entity is already used by another appliance or EV charger.
errors.unknown_device: The device no longer exists in Home Assistant.
errors.entity_not_on_device: The entity does not belong to the device of the EV charger, or to the device of the appliance's switch.
errors.invalid_action: Home Assistant cannot read the action.
errors.invalid_template: The template has a syntax error.
errors.default_action_unavailable: The entity has no standard action. Choose custom actions.
errors.unsupported_entity_domain: This type of entity cannot be used here. Choose one from the list.
errors.domain_action_unavailable: The action is not available for the entity. Choose another action.
errors.unsupported_option: The entity does not support this value.
errors.outside_entity_range: Outside the range of the entity.
errors.current_off_unsupported: The entity cannot be set to 0 A, which stops an EV charger turned on and off by the current.
errors.essential_with_variants: An essential appliance cannot have variants. Delete them, or turn the setting off.
errors.essential_with_power_reserve: An essential appliance has no power reserve. Turn the setting off, or turn off Fixed load first.
errors.essential_not_at_top: An essential appliance must be above every other entry in the priority list.
errors.not_a_thermostat: Choose a thermostat, a climate entity.

power_sensor.label: Power sensor
power_sensor.helper: The power the whole house uses, usually from the HAN port of the electricity meter.

regulation_window_s.label: Regulation window
regulation_window_s.helper: A longer window evens out short peaks, a shorter one reacts faster. Default {default} s.

power_sensor_timeout_s.label: Power sensor timeout
power_sensor_timeout_s.helper: When the power sensor has not reported for this long, everything is turned off until it is back. Filled in from how the power sensor reports when it is chosen. {min}–{max} s.

power_limit_w.label: Power limit
power_limit_w.helper: The step in the capacity tariff you want to stay below. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W.

turn_on_margin_w.label: Turn-on margin
turn_on_margin_w.helper: How far below the power limit consumption must be before anything is turned on. A larger margin means less switching. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W.

wait_at_limit_s.label: Waiting time at the power limit
wait_at_limit_s.helper: How long an appliance waits before it is turned on when consumption is close to the power limit. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

penalty_threshold_w.label: Penalty threshold
penalty_threshold_w.helper: How far the consumption over the last hour may go above the power limit before everything is turned off until the overconsumption is paid back. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W.

appliance_repeat_increment_factor.label: Increase each time
appliance_repeat_increment_factor.helper: Share of the waiting time at the power limit. Default × {default}.

ampere_damping_s.label: Damping time
ampere_damping_s.helper: How long an EV charger waits before it gets back an ampere it lost. Longer gives steadier consumption, shorter more charging. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

charger_waiting_factor.label: Waiting time for EV chargers
charger_waiting_factor.helper: How many times longer than an appliance an EV charger waits before it is activated again. {min}×–{max}×, default {default}×.

action_timeout_s.label: Action timeout
action_timeout_s.helper: An action that takes longer is stopped. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

general.penalty_info: A safety valve for when consumption gets far above the power limit, for example when something outside Kraftvakt is turned on.

reports.title: Timing of the measurements
reports.description: How often and how evenly the measurements have come over the last hour, and what that gives with the settings above.
reports.no_power_sensor: Choose the power sensor to see how it reports.
reports.analysing: Finding out how the power sensor reports. It can take up to 30 seconds.
reports.not_analysed: Could not find out how the power sensor reports.
reports.no_updates: The power sensor has not reported yet. Kraftvakt decides by its own clock until it does.
reports.not_known: The power sensor has not reported often enough yet to tell how it reports. Kraftvakt decides by its own clock every {window} s meanwhile.
reports.steady_one: Reports every {interval} s, steadily: one measurement per regulation window, with a decision right after it.
reports.steady: Reports every {interval} s, steadily: {updates} measurements per regulation window, with a decision right after the last measurement.
reports.steady_longer: Reports every {interval} s, steadily: {updates} measurements per regulation window, which then lasts {seconds} s, with a decision right after the last measurement.
reports.varies: Reports at uneven intervals, from {shortest} to {longest} s. The HAN reader probably reports only when the power changes, as readers on a radio network such as Zigbee often do. Kraftvakt keeps the last value between reports, and decides by its own clock every {window} s.
reports.steadier: For a steadier regulation, set the maximum report interval of the HAN reader to 10 s or less.
reports.longer_than_window: The power sensor reports every {interval} s, less often than the regulation window, so each regulation window lasts {seconds} s, until the next report. Choose {choice} s or longer.
reports.seldom: Up to {longest} s between reports. A change in consumption can then be seen that late, and the power limit may be exceeded meanwhile. Set the maximum report interval of the HAN reader to 10 s or less.
reports.near_timeout: Up to {longest} s between reports, close to the power sensor timeout of {timeout} s. If the reader is silent longer, everything is turned off as if it had stopped. Set the maximum report interval of the HAN reader lower, or raise the timeout.

advanced.wait_curve_info: How long an appliance waits, by how much power is free. The actual waiting time is rounded up to the next decision.
advanced.repeated_turn_on_info: The waiting time grows when the same appliance is turned on again and again. The first two times follow the curve, shown at the pivot point.
advanced.chargers_info: Keeps an EV charger from going up and down, or on and off, when consumption changes for a short moment.
advanced.command_repeat_info: Sets appliances and EV chargers back if they have changed by themselves, for example after a power cut.
advanced.timeouts_info: Guards against actions that never finish.

appliances.priority_sub: Highest priority at the top. Drag to change the order.
appliances.empty: No appliances yet. Add the ones Kraftvakt shall turn on and off.

appliance.variants_info: Gives the appliance another place in the priority list while the expression is true, for example higher up for the water heater in the morning. The top variant that applies is used.
appliance.display_values_info: Optional. Shown only on the status page.

entity_id.label: Switch or thermostat
entity_id.helper: What Kraftvakt turns on and off, for example the switch of the water heater.

essential.label: Essential appliance
essential.helper: For an appliance that must always run, such as a freezer. Cannot have variants.

fixed_load.label: Fixed load
fixed_load.helper: For an appliance that always uses the same power while it is on, such as a ceiling fan. It is turned on without waiting when enough power is free. Not for one with a thermostat or other control of its own.

power_reserve_w.label: Power reserve
power_reserve_w.helper: What the appliance uses while it is on. Applies to every variant.

variant.condition_info: The variant applies while the expression is true, for example between 05 and 08.

action.entity_runs: Runs {service} for the chosen entity with the current as value.
action.no_default: This type of entity has no standard action. Use custom actions.
action.choose_entity: Choose the entity to use the standard action.
action.choose_action_entity: Choose the number entity that gets the charging current.
action.source_no_value: No temperature now: the action fails while it has none.
action.source_range: Read when the action runs, and kept within {min}–{max} {unit}.

condition.state_helper: For example a sensor that shows the status of the EV charger.
condition.template_helper: Should give true or false. Variables: {variables}.
condition.invalid: The template gives {value}, not true or false, so it counts as false.

one_at_a_time.entity_helper: One EV charger at a time while it is on.
one_at_a_time.template_helper: True gives one EV charger at a time, for example {{ power_limit < 15000 }}. Variables: {variables}.
one_at_a_time.invalid: The template gives {value}, not true or false, so the EV chargers charge several at once.

actively_charging.state_helper: For example a sensor that shows the status of the EV charger.
actively_charging.template_helper: True while the car charges. Variables: {variables}.
actively_charging.invalid: The template gives {value}, not true or false, so it counts as not charging.

charging_power.power_sensor_helper: What the car charges with now.
charging_power.invalid: The template gives {value}, not a number, so it counts as not charging.

display_power.power_sensor_helper: A sensor of the same device as the switch or thermostat.
display_power.template_helper: The power in W, also from another device. Variables: {variables}.
display_power.invalid: The template gives {value}, not a number, so nothing is shown.

display_temperature.temperature_sensor_helper: From the same device as the switch or thermostat.
display_temperature.template_helper: The temperature in the unit of Home Assistant, also from another device. Variables: {variables}.
display_temperature.invalid: The template gives {value}, not a number, so nothing is shown.

fault.state_helper: For example a sensor that shows the status of the EV charger.
fault.invalid: The template gives {value}, not true or false, so it counts as no fault.

charging.name: Name
charging.name_sub: Shown in the priority list and on the status page.
charging.one_at_a_time: Restrict to one EV charger at a time
charging.one_at_a_time_sub: Only one car in the group charges at a time, so it is full sooner.
charging.dynamic_order_sub: Cars that charge keep charging, and the others wait their turn.
charging.needs_two_chargers: Applies only with two or more EV chargers in the group.
charging.chargers_sub: Highest priority at the top. Drag an EV charger to another group to move it.
charging.no_groups: No groups of EV chargers yet. Add a group, and then its EV chargers.
charging.delete_group_not_empty: Move or delete its EV chargers to delete the group.
charging.switches_info: While the regulation runs, you can control each EV charger with the switches «‹charger› excluded from regulation», «‹charger› override charging window» and «‹charger› charge until car disconnected».
charging.charges_until_disconnected: charges until the car is disconnected

charger.start_info: How long the car may take to start charging after the EV charger is activated.
charger.on_off_info: How Kraftvakt activates and deactivates the EV charger.
charger.switched_by_current_info: Choose the entity or action that sets the current under Charging current. It must take 0 A.
charger.profile_applied: Filled in from the charger profile {profile}. Check every field before you save.

override_ends.charging_stopped: When the car no longer charges

device_id.label: Device
device_id.helper: The EV charger in Home Assistant. When Kraftvakt knows the charger, the fields below are filled in.

on_off_entity.label: Switch that allows charging
on_off_entity.helper: Turned on to activate the EV charger and off to deactivate it.

min_current_power_w.label: Power at minimum current
min_current_power_w.helper: What the car uses at the minimum current, about 1,400 W on one phase. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W, 6 A on three phases.

car_connected.label: Car connected
car_connected.helper: Tells whether a car is connected to the EV charger.

actively_charging.label: Actively charging
actively_charging.helper: The charging power tells how much the car uses. «Car charging» is optional, and may tell sooner that the car has started charging.

cloud_controlled.label: Cloud-controlled EV charger
cloud_controlled.helper: For an EV charger controlled through a cloud service. Kraftvakt then sends it fewer commands.

deactivate_on_fault.label: Deactivate on fault
deactivate_on_fault.helper: Stops the EV charger while it has a fault, so the others in the group may charge.

charging_window.label: Charging window
charging_window.helper: The EV charger charges only within this time each day, for example at night.

charge_until_disconnected.label: Charge until the car is disconnected
charge_until_disconnected.helper: A car that has started charging within the charging window may go on charging after it ends.

override_ends.label: End the override
override_ends.helper: When the switch «‹charger› override charging window» turns itself off.

charger.charging_current_info: The minimum is the lowest current the car charges with, usually 6 A, and the maximum what the EV charger and its fuse allow.

switched_by.current: The charging current, where 0 A stops charging
